 The main turbine, also known as the power turbine, is the component of a steam turbine system that converts the thermal energy of steam into mechanical energy. It consists of several key components:

1. Rotor: The rotating component of the turbine, which consists of a rotor disc and a set of rotor blades.
2. Stator: The stationary component of the turbine, which consists of a stator casing and a set of stator blades.
3. Nozzles: The components that direct the high-pressure steam onto the buckets.
4. Buckets: The components that capture the thermal energy from the steam and convert it into mechanical energy.
5. Turbine driven oil pump: A pump that is driven by the turbine to supply lubrication to the journal and thrust bearings.
6. Journal bearings: Thin, lubricated bearings that support the rotor on its axial and radial loads.
7. Thrust bearings: Thick, lubricated bearings that support the rotor on its axial loads, located at the rear of the rotor.
8. Foundation (pedestal): The component that supports the entire turbine and is bolted to the turbine condenser exhaust flange.
9. Keys: Metal components that fit into keyways in the rotor disc to prevent rotation and ensure alignment.
10. Bolting: The process of securing the turbine to the foundation using bolts.
11. Couplings: Components that connect the turbine to the rest of the system, allowing for rotational speed and torque differences.
12. Steam seals: Components that prevent leakage of steam from the turbine to the surroundings.
13. Insulation: Materials that are used to insulate the turbine and prevent heat loss.
14. Appearance lagging: Materials that are used to provide thermal protection and reduce noise.
